How to Calculate AFCAT Marks?

To calculate your AFCAT marks, you need to understand the marking system. The exam has 100 questions. Each correct answer gives you 3 marks, and 1 mark is deducted for every wrong answer. Follow these simple steps:

  1. Count how many questions you answered correctly.
  2. Multiply the number of correct answers by 3.
  3. Count how many questions you answered incorrectly.
  4. Multiply the number of wrong answers by 1.
  5. Subtract the negative marks for wrong answers from the total marks you got for correct answers.

AFCAT 1 Cut Off 2026

The AFCAT Cut Off 2026 is released along with the result. Candidates can check their category wise cut off through the AFCAT 1 Cut Off PDF. The cut-off is the minimum number of marks needed to pass the exam and move to the next stage. The cut-off changes every year depending on the exam difficulty and number of vacancies. Separate cut-offs are announced for AFCAT 1 and Engineering Knowledge Test.

What After AFCAT 1 Result 2026?

After the AFCAT result is declared, candidates who qualify are called for the Air Force Selection Board tests. These tests include psychological tests, group activities and personal interviews.

Candidates who clear this stage must go through a medical examination. After that, a final merit list is prepared based on AFCAT marks, AFSB performance and medical fitness. Selected candidates will get training at the Air Force Academy and become officers after successfully completing the training.

AFCAT 1 2026 Result FAQs

Q1. When will the AFCAT result come in 2026?

Ans. The AFCAT 1 result 2026 has been released on 11th March 2026 on the official website.

Q2. Where can I check the AFCAT Result 2026?

Ans. Candidates can check their AFCAT 1 result 2026 on www.afcat.edcil.co.in.

Q3. What happens after AFCAT 1 Result 2026?

Ans. Candidates qualified in written test will be called for AFSB testing followed by medical examination and final merit list.

Q4. How many times is AFCAT conducted every year?

Ans. The AFCAT exam is conducted twice every year as AFCAT 1 and AFCAT 2. It is conducted twice to provide candidates with multiple opportunities to join the Indian Air Force.
